name: Fluorouracil cream (Efudex)

lead: Fluorouracil (5-FU) cream is a topical chemotherapy agent that dermatologists prescribe for actinic keratosis, the rough sun-damaged patches that can precede skin cancer. It is also used for superficial skin cancers and warts.

For appearance it clears scaly lesions and, as shown in research on topical treatment, leaves skin that has gone through a red, peeling phase. Trials compare it with other lesion treatments; studies of its cosmetic effects are limited.

paras: It is applied to affected areas of skin for a course set by a clinician, during which skin typically becomes red, crusted and sore before healing. Dermatologists may adjust frequency to manage the reaction.

Common effects are pain, burning, crusting, redness and swelling at the site, and Wikipedia notes pigment change or scarring is possible; severe toxicity occurs in people with DPD deficiency with systemic use. A case report describes ectropion after eyelid-area use. It is prescription-only.

chain: Abnormal cells are destroyed in an inflamed phase
Healing skin is smoother and clearer
angle.text: It removes scaly precancerous spots in a clinician-guided course. Appearance changes come after a visible reaction, and its main purpose is medical.

lead: Fluorouracil cream, sold under brand names including Efudex, is a topical form of the chemotherapy drug 5-FU. It blocks DNA and RNA synthesis in abnormal fast-dividing skin cells and is widely used for actinic keratoses, superficial skin cancers and warts. [1][2]

For looks, the relevance is in clearing sun-damaged patches and lesions: actinic keratoses are rough, scaly spots, and treated areas go through an inflamed, peeling stage before healing. [1][2] Randomised trials have compared 5-FU cream with other lesion treatments such as KOH solution, and in plantar warts with salicylic acid, liquid nitrogen and imiquimod. [3][4] Case series have also tested it for vitiligo patches under occlusion, reporting repigmentation in many treated patients. [5][6]
infobox: Actinic keratosis, superficial skin cancers, warts

paras: Actinic keratoses convert to squamous cell carcinoma at about 0.25-1% per year by one review's estimate, and local destruction or topical agents are standard options. [1] Wikipedia lists topical 5-FU for actinic keratosis, basal cell carcinoma, Bowen's disease and warts. [2]

A 1983 controlled series applied 5% fluorouracil under occlusion after abrasion to vitiligo lesions in 28 patients; 64% showed complete or near-complete repigmentation, and 3 of 23 responders relapsed within a year. [5] A newer trial combined 5-FU with microneedling in stable vitiligo. [6]

A randomised trial compared 5% KOH solution with 5-FU cream in actinic keratoses. [3] A pragmatic multicentre trial compared salicylic acid, liquid nitrogen, 5-FU cream and imiquimod in previously treated plantar warts. [4] See also the vitiligo studies above. [5][6]
Pain, itching, burning, crusting and dermatitis are common topically, with possible pigment changes or scarring. [2] A case report describes ectropion following topical use. [7]

Charles Heidelberger asked Hoffmann-La Roche to synthesise fluorouracil after earlier work on liver tumour uptake of uracil; it was patented in 1956, reported in 1957 and entered medical use in 1962. [2]

timeline.event: Tumour inhibition in mice is reported. [2]
